note: T003 of feature 148. The NAMES a command of a check may see outside the `parity` profile. The environment of a command is this allow-list, overlaid with the `env` the command declares (F148-FR-002); under the `parity` profile it is the environment of the process overlaid with the declared `env`, as at the baseline (DV-113, row 125 of annex X §X.7). The list holds no provider credential: control T-21 of `packages/contracts/data/threat-model.json` ("A check runs repository code with the runtime's environment" — "A scrubbed environment, no provider key"); `research.md` D-8.

allow.name: PATH
allow.reason: The search path a check resolves its tools with. Its value is the one recorded at launch, not the live value of the process (F148-FR-010).

allow.name: HOME
allow.reason: A toolchain that cannot read a home directory fails for a reason that is not the check.

allow.name: TMPDIR
allow.reason: The temporary directory of the command. The runner sets it to the command's own directory, which is removed after the result was taken (plan.md, Storage).

allow.name: LANG
allow.reason: Without it a toolchain may order or render output by the locale of the host, and two runs of the same check would differ.

allow.name: LC_ALL
allow.reason: The same reason as LANG, and it overrides every other LC_ variable, so one name is enough.

allow.name: TZ
allow.reason: A check that prints a timestamp prints the same one on every host.

allow.name: CI
allow.reason: A toolchain that reads it turns off its progress output and its colour, which keeps the captured output stable under the cap.

allow.name: TERM
allow.reason: A toolchain that finds no terminal writes plain output. The runner sets the value `dumb` for the same reason.

allow.name: NO_COLOR
allow.reason: Escape sequences in captured output are not the result of the check and consume the cap.

allow.name: SYSTEMROOT
allow.reason: On Windows a process without it cannot resolve a socket or a DLL. On Linux and macOS the name is absent and the entry adds nothing.

forbidden.note: Names that MUST NOT be in `allow`, whatever the environment of the runtime holds. The four exact names are the provider variables of `packages/config/data/alias-table.json`; the patterns catch a provider credential the alias table does not yet name. A name of the environment that matches a pattern is dropped even when it is not in this list.
